sights.w: The public building Apple built across the street from its 'spaceship' ring HQ, opened 2017. A design landmark in its own right, with a carbon-fiber roof floating on stone columns.
sights.k: Open to anyone: full Apple Store, Caffe Macs rooftop cafe/terrace with a distant view over the ring, and an augmented-reality tabletop model of the campus. The ring building itself and the grounds are closed to the public.

sights.n: Steve Jobs' Childhood Home & Apple Garage
sights.w: The ranch house where Steve Jobs grew up and where he and Steve Wozniak built the first Apple I computers in the garage in 1976. Los Altos designated it a historic resource in 2013.
sights.k: View from the public street ONLY. It is a private, occupied residence with no plaque or tour; do not enter the property or disturb residents. Just a quiet curbside pilgrimage.

sights.address: 2000 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
sights.w: Google's official public front door at the Googleplex, opened October 2023 inside the striking curved 'Gradient Canopy' (Charleston East) building. The rest of the Googleplex is closed to non-employees.
sights.k: Open to the public: the Google Store (hardware + exclusive branded merch), a cafe, the Huddle event space and an outdoor Plaza with public art. Offices and the wider campus are off-limits.

sights.address: Charleston Rd & Huff Ave, Mountain View, CA 94043
sights.w: The beloved oversized foam sculptures of Android dessert mascots (Cupcake through Pie, etc.). The tradition ran 2008-2019; newer versions are digital-only.
sights.k: An outdoor photo spot beside the Google Visitor Experience. The statues were moved here from the old Landings Drive lawn (redeveloped) in 2022; the area is technically for Google employees and guests, but visitors are generally welcomed to walk up and photograph them. Best combined with a Visitor Experience stop.

sights.address: 1401 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
sights.w: The world's leading museum of computing history, holding everything from a working Babbage Difference Engine reconstruction to Cray supercomputers and a restored PDP-1. A must for any tech traveler.
sights.k: Fully open to the public (Wed-Sun, ~10a-5p; general admission ~$15). No membership or affiliation needed.

sights.address: 2200 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054
sights.w: A free museum at Intel's HQ tracing the silicon-chip story from the transistor to modern processors, with hands-on exhibits on how chips are made and Intel's Silicon Valley founding.
sights.k: Free and open to the public inside the Robert Noyce Building lobby (Mon-Fri, ~9a-5p; call ahead as it closes for events). The rest of the Intel campus is not public.

sights.address: 2788 San Tomas Expy, Santa Clara, CA 95051
sights.w: NVIDIA's dramatic triangle-motif headquarters: the Gensler-designed Endeavor (2017) and the enormous Voyager (2022), whose sloped glass 'mountain' roof shelters an indoor landscaped village.
sights.k: Exterior architecture only. The buildings are private and closed to the public; the striking hexagonal/triangular forms are best appreciated from the sidewalk and San Tomas Expressway. No visitor center or tours.

sights.n: HP Garage - Birthplace of Silicon Valley
sights.w: The one-car garage where Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard started Hewlett-Packard in 1939, widely honored as the birthplace of Silicon Valley. California Historical Landmark and on the National Register.
sights.k: View from the public sidewalk ONLY. It is a private HP-owned property, not open inside; a bronze plaque on the front lawn reads 'Birthplace of Silicon Valley.'

sights.address: 3333 Coyote Hill Rd, Palo Alto, CA 94304
sights.w: The low-slung research lab (now PARC, part of SRI International) where the graphical user interface, the mouse, Ethernet, laser printing and WYSIWYG editing were invented in the 1970s - ideas that shaped every modern computer.
sights.k: Exterior/landmark only. It is a working private research facility, not open to the public; the site sits on Coyote Hill above Stanford with hiking-trail views nearby. A pilgrimage for the story, not the building.

sights.n: NASA Ames Exploration Center & Hangar One
sights.w: NASA's free space-science visitor center at Ames Research Center/Moffett Field, with Mercury and Apollo-era artifacts, a Mars meteorite and moon-mission exhibits. Nearby looms Hangar One, the colossal 1930s airship hangar that is a Bay Area landmark.
sights.k: The Exploration Center sits outside the security gate and is free and open to the public (Tue-Fri 10a-4p, Sat-Sun 12-4p) - no base access needed. Hangar One and the airfield itself are secured; the hangar is viewable from outside/afar only. (The separate Moffett Field Museum, inside the gate, requires ID and a fee.)

sights.w: The famous sign at the entrance to Meta's (Facebook's) headquarters - once the giant blue thumbs-up 'Like', now the blue Meta infinity logo (swapped in the 2021 rebrand). A classic Silicon Valley selfie stop.
sights.k: Photo stop at the entrance sign ONLY, from the public roadside. The Meta campus is closed to the public - no walk-in access. The famous thumbs-up is gone; the sign now shows the Meta infinity mark (with 'Facebook' still on the reverse).

sights.address: 151 S Almaden Blvd, San Jose, CA 95113
sights.w: Adobe's cluster of towers that anchors downtown San Jose's skyline. Atop the Almaden Tower is the 'San Jose Semaphore,' a public art installation of four rotating LED disks that broadcast an encoded message.
sights.k: Exterior and skyline only - the offices are private. The San Jose Semaphore art piece is visible free from the street/downtown after dark (message decodable online). No public interior or tours.

sights.w: The headquarters campus of eBay, one of the dot-com era's defining companies, whose whimsical signage and 'Main Street' welcome center reflect its marketplace roots.
sights.k: Exterior and signage only. The campus is a private workplace not open to the public; the branded eBay sign and buildings can be seen from the roadside.

sights.address: 3655 N First St, San Jose, CA 95134
sights.w: Samsung's striking 10-story North American semiconductor HQ (opened 2015), a LEED-Platinum tower with a sculptural stepped facade - the standout landmark of North San Jose's 'Golden Triangle' tech corridor along N First St, which also hosts PayPal, Cisco and others.
sights.k: Exterior architecture and signage only. The building is a private office, not open to the public; admire the facade from N First St. Neighboring PayPal (2211 N First St) and Cisco (170 W Tasman Dr) campuses are likewise exteriors-only drive-bys.
